1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 g6 4.c3 a6 5.Ba4.strategy: Hits e5 a second time, and with the c6 knight pinned by the bishop on a4 the pawn is genuinely under threat. White takes central space; Black must unpin or exchange.
Breaks the pin on the c6 knight, the key defender of e5, before White can exploit it. Black keeps the kingside fianchetto set-up, a solid and flexible position, and accepts a slight lack of space.
